assertions.name: the_parametrisation_reproduces_the_census_cell
assertions.source: the (slot, kind) coordinates used here reproduce the census witness's tr_conv_D to 1.41e-26: the census assignment is p = (0, 'sigma'), n = (2, 'inv'). Without this the whole enumeration would be about a different object -- the check whose absence caused this branch's earlier retraction

assertions.name: the_one_letter_freedom_is_four_distinct_elements
assertions.source: slots 0 and 1 are both generator 0 and give exactly the same trace (agreement < 1.0e-25), so the 6 (slot, kind) configurations realise only 4 distinct traces: ['0.475133517156', '0.558733065217', '0.629328402203', '0.712927950264']. Only the GENERATOR of the odd letter matters, not its slot within a generator

assertions.name: bar_parity_narrows_the_freedom_and_EXCLUDES_the_census_assignment
assertions.source: requiring tr^{z_D}(Delta)(1/q) = -tr^{z_D}(Delta)(q) leaves 8 of the 26 ordered (p, n) pairs with p != n, and the census assignment p = (0, 'sigma'), n = (2, 'inv') is NOT among them. Every surviving pair gives both nucleons the SAME member of the bar-pair and differs only in generator; the census gives them OPPOSITE members, which is exactly what breaks the parity

assertions.name: the_eight_survivors_collapse_to_ONE_magnitude_by_an_exact_identity
assertions.source: Delta(sigma, sigma) = -Delta(inv, inv) EXACTLY (symbolic: simplify(Ds + Di) == 0), so all 8 bar-odd pairs share one |tr(Delta)| -- measured, 1 distinct magnitude. There is therefore NOTHING to select among the survivors, which is what keeps this a derivation rather than a choice

assertions.name: the_forced_value_is_WORSE_than_the_census_and_that_is_the_point
assertions.source: the bar-odd constraint forces Q_beta = 0.353415697967 MeV, -54.825437 %, against the census assignment's -16.67794 %. The derived answer is the less accurate one. AGENTS.md: implement the specification and report what it gives even when that is worse; rank by derivational cleanliness, never by residual. No configuration was chosen for its value -- the constraint is a parity in q and the survivors collapse

assertions.name: no_configuration_is_whole_element_PSD_feasible_reading_B_only
assertions.source: all 6 (slot, kind) configurations FAIL Matrix.PosSemidef on at least one Wedderburn block -- the census assignment and every bar-odd alternative alike. 🛑 THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A REJECTION BY THE RULING: the SDP scope question was answered '(A) core only' (bean qou-99qc, 2026-09-12), under which reading 3 constrains 6 of the 11 letters and prunes NOTHING among the 5 the parity bound leaves free. Applying PSD to the WHOLE element is reading (B), which was not selected. So the SDP half does no work on these letters either way, and the bar-odd constraint above is the ONLY derived handle on them

description: The gamma-gamma ruling provably cannot reach 5 of the 11 letters, and of those the whole p/n asymmetry sits in ONE quark letter. Imposing the corpus's own bar-odd property for Q_beta (AGENTS.md line 2182) on the ruled z_D base narrows the 26 non-degenerate ordered (p, n) pairs to 8, and the CENSUS ASSIGNMENT IS NOT AMONG THEM -- every bar-odd pair gives both nucleons the same member of the bar-pair, the census gives them opposite members. The 8 then COLLAPSE: Delta(sigma,sigma) = -Delta(inv,inv) exactly, so |tr(Delta)| is one number and no selection is possible or needed. It gives Q_beta = 0.353415698 MeV, -54.825 % -- WORSE than the census -16.678 %, which is the point: derived beats selected. It does NOT close Q_beta: all four distinct elements fail PSD, so the SDP half rejects the whole family. Scope-(a); conditional on the bar-odd property transferring from the retired z = 1 cell.
